items.summary: Related: Verification Theater: Measured Failure Modes of AI Verifier Panels , accepted (poster) at the NeurIPS 2026 workshop Who Verifies the Agents? Version of record: SSRN 7653679 , DOI 10.2139/ssrn.7653679 . Cite that version. The same text is also at polyhelper.ai/research/sealed-before-the-open/ and https://github.com/vadimchernets/papers/tree/main/sealed-before-the-open . The registered predictions of Section 8 are on OSF: 10.17605/OSF.IO/9Q86N . The immutable release of the open league files on which every number of the paper rests: 10.5281/zenodo.23552700 . The live league and its open data (CC BY 4.0): trends.polyhelper.ai/markets , trends.polyhelper.ai/api/v1 . This deposit is an archival copy made so that the full text stays retrievable; it makes no separate claim. When an AI model says gold will rise, anyone can score the call at the close, but few can check when it was made. A backtest mixes memory with skill, and an operator's log asks for trust. I propose a standard for measuring AI market forecasts, written as a ladder of checkable requirements, and I run its reference implementation, AI Council · Markets: an open league where fourteen models, seven from US and seven from Chinese laboratories, face one question on one price snapshot. Before each New York open the ten on its Council, five from each side, give probabilities for twelve indicators at four horizons. Each answer is sealed into a hash chain before the price it is scored from, the chain is anchored in Bitcoin and signed by independent time-stamping authorities, and one run per session counts by a rule declared in advance. On 21 October 2026, the first counted morning, every counted answer was signed before the 09:30 ET open. Agreement among the models proved to be a count of independent voices, not a headcount: on two development mornings the seven and eight models sealed before the open were as alike as about 1.6 independent forecasters, nine counted ones were worth 2.23, and the closest pairs crossed the US-China line. Check a seal with three commands, and score my thirty predictions, registered on OSF, before I do.
items.title: Sealed Before the Open: A Verifiable Standard for Measuring AI Forecasts of Financial Markets

items.summary: NANOSENSING ACUPUNCTURE AND ACUPOINT MICROENVIRONMENT METROLOGY AT THE LIMIT STARLI / WHITE RAINBOW EPOCH / 33 x STARLI ORIGINAL CIVILIZATIONAL INTERPRETATION This English-language prospective research monograph asks whether historically nominated acupuncture points exhibit reproducible paired differences in local electrical impedance or optically inferred superficial tissue oxygenation when compared with anatomically and environmentally matched nonpoint sites. Its core three-coupling is Acupoint Microenvironments x Multimodal Metrology x Paired Control. The principal White Rainbow Epoch Hypothesis is deliberately vulnerable to refutation: analysts blinded to point identity must be able to reconstruct an independently calibrated advantage when equally hydrated measurement sites are exchanged under a concealed test condition. Skin water content, contact pressure, temperature, electrode polarization, ordinary neurovascular anatomy, skin pigmentation, photon pathlength and site-selection bias are treated as strong competing explanations, not minor caveats. The civilizational purpose follows a governing three-coupling: Continuity of Chinese Cultural Heritage x Exploration through Modern Science x Original Civilizational Interpretation of the White Rainbow Epoch. Classical acupuncture, Chinese medical philosophy, yin-yang, Five Phases and Daoist thought are welcomed as inherited cultural frameworks capable of generating questions. They are not relabelled novel SI-measurable energy fields or independently validated clinical mechanisms. Established physical laws and metrological statistics likewise remain inherited knowledge rather than purported discoveries by 33 x STARLI. Newly composed, falsifiable interdisciplinary proposals are marked White Rainbow Epoch Hypotheses. Cultural interpretation may remain meaningful even when a particular physical hypothesis fails. The book contains 30 mechanism-distinct golden mathematical plates, 82 scientific chapters and 410 individually paginated research investigations, 200 one-page Research Gates whose large deep-navy opening questions lead to discriminating experiments, and 33 scientifically distinguishable Phoenix Answer Embryos. The plates include complex impedance, electrode polarization, pressure and hydration sensitivity, optical pathlength, chromophore inversion, heat transport, oxygen diffusion, spatial statistics, hierarchical and covariance-aware inference, multiplicity, null-equivalence and hard integrity vetoes. The Gates present concrete blinded challenges, resource-matched traditional metrology baselines, necessary calibration and acceptance margins, failure pathways and independent handoff requirements. Each Phoenix embryo has a different named instrument or provisional mechanism, adversarial test, rival explanation and honest metamorphosis path when rejected. The editorial DOI scope is intentionally limited to three author-associated STARLI mother research volumes: 10.5281/zenodo.23480803 (AI Microrobotic Sensing of Senescent-Cell Heterogeneity at the Limit), 10.5281/zenodo.23486020 (Reconfigurable Robotic Swarms and Continuous Functional Regeneration at the Limit), and 10.5281/zenodo.23318840 (Microrobotic Sampling and Quantum Biosensing Co-Design at the Limit). Their chapter lineages offer methodological ancestry in measurement provenance, bias governance, independent requalification and sample-state preservation. They are not independent evidence that the proposed acupoint effect exists. The project does not exclude established scientific knowledge or ancient philosophy; it simply does not include other authors' DOI records in this particular bibliography.

items.summary: Background/Objectives : With the advent of the current digital health age, opportunities for interacting with health systems have grown not only more frequent but also variable in type, spanning across emergent care settings, routine outpatient follow-up, as well as at-home telemedicine-based platforms. In light of initiatives to re-design electronic medical records (EMR) to more meaningfully curate evidence-based insights, our research objective is focused on harnessing underutilized data features (i.e., time-ordered events) to map the complex interactions that patients undergo within their health systems. We posit that inclusion of information associated with sequential patterns will help more accurately simulate care pathways and outcomes. We report preliminary data on care utilization patterns among cohorts of patients diagnosed with chronic disease. Methods : De-identified data were extracted from the MedStar Health AIM-AHEAD Data Bridge (AADB)’s Chronic Disease repository. EMRs were queried for patients with confirmed diagnoses for diabetes mellitus (ICD-10: E10.X or E11.X) as well as heart failure (ICD-10: I50.X). For each unique patient, encounters related to care utilization were sequentially collated, with explicit demarcation of whether interactions occurred before or after corresponding diagnoses. For analytical purposes, encounters were categorized as “Emergency”, “Inpatient”, “Observation”, “Outpatient”, “Home Health”, and “Patient Portal”. For each cohort, sequential pattern mining (SPM) was used to generate antecedent-consequent prediction rules and calculate the conditional probabilities (confidence) of subsequent care utilization episodes. Analyses were performed using R (The R Foundation for Statistical Computing; version 4.5.2). Results : Between January 2018 and December 2024, we distinctly identified 202,605 patients with a diagnosis for diabetes mellitus as well as 79,223 patients with a diagnosis for heart failure. Across both cohorts, 42,208 patients had documentation of being diagnosed with both conditions and were flagged separately for potential sensitivity analyses. The proportion of older patients (50 years or above) was predominant (>85% for all patients). The median number of annual healthcare interactions tended to increase post-diagnosis (versus pre-diagnosis) particularly in diabetic cohorts: 3.0 versus 1.0 (diabetes only); 5.0 versus 1.7 (diabetes and heart failure). Total instances of care episodes (t) were enumerated across the 7-year study period: diabetes only (t=3,511,417), heart failure only (t=741,789), diabetes and heart failure (t=1,681,307). SPM algorithms were used to generate rulebooks associating unique care utilization patterns with their corresponding likelihood of subsequent events. Discussion/Conclusions : Our initial findings highlight a wide variability of care utilization patterns among patients diagnosed with chronic diseases. We demonstrated that analyzing care utilization sequences may yield embedded insights that can be harnessed for prospectively tracking person-centered health trajectories. The current work exhibits several limitations and opportunities for expanded analysis. We expect to enrich our data pipeline with more detailed clinical features (e.g., medications, laboratory panels, procedures) in future iterations. This comprehensive ingestion would enable the initial steps towards developing models for predicting the onset of unfavorable health outcomes. Implications: Notwithstanding these considerations, the goals of our preliminary efforts are aligned with learning health systems models which emphasize the implementation of evidence-based insights at the point-of-care. With increasing integration of multi-modal sources of longitudinal health information as well as availability of high-computing resources, connected health technologies may serve as valuable applications from whi

items.summary: RASHER begins as a fork of BACoN 0.4.0 (commit 4fdec16, which includes the samtools consensus -C 20 change below), adapted to Illumina short reads. Everything under "BACoN changelog" is the parent tool's history, kept for provenance. Changed Renamed throughout: the package, command, log ( rasher.log ) and lock file ( .rasher.lock ) are rasher . The pipeline reads Illumina short reads , paired or single-end. sample_R1 / sample_R2 , sample_1 / _2 sample.R1 / .R2 and sample.1 / .2 files (bcl2fastq _001 tails included) pair into one sample, in flat folders, subfolders and sample sheets; a file without a mate is a single-end sample, and unmated files next to a sample's pairs are skipped with a warning. A pair is baited whole when either mate matches the reference, mates travel together through every step ( 1_extracted/<sample>_R1/_R2 , 2_filtered/... ), and a desynchronised pair is an error, whether the mates carry identical names or /1 /2 suffixes. Baiting aligns with minimap2 -x sr (BBDuk baits pairs natively with in2= / outm2= ). --keep-bam now keeps the baited reads aligned to the reference (paired samples: a proper paired BAM). Filtering: fastp (adapter trimming, quality and length filters; its JSON and HTML reports land in logs/2_filter/ where MultiQC finds them) followed by deterministic, evenly spread subsampling of the reads (pairs kept whole) to --target-depth . Filtlong, --keep-percent and --filter-by-reference are gone; --min-read-length defaults to 50. Fasta reads skip fastp and are filtered by length. Templated assembly aligns pairs with minimap2 -ax sr and calls samtools consensus -X hiseq (call quality at least 20, as BACoN's unreleased change at the time of the fork). De novo assembly: SKESA ( -a skesa ; the recommended de novo assembler — on the real-data benchmark its SNP distances matched SPAdes' with far fewer contigs) or SPAdes ( -a spades , --isolate ; writes the assembly graph, more robust below ~30x depth). Flye and myloasm are gone, with --read-type and --min-size . --snp-method auto is minimap2 for templated assemblies and SKA2 for SPAdes and SKESA assemblies. -m/--memory also sizes SPAdes and SKESA (it was BBDuk-only). A paired sample X next to a sample named X_R1 or X_R2 is an error (their outputs would collide). No assembler flags circular contigs any more, so SKA2's circular-contig end extension no longer applies. Single-end extraction matches read names with a trailing /1 or /2 stripped, as aligners report them. Output folders of BACoN do not resume under RASHER (the checkpoint fingerprints are seeded with the tool's name; every step runs again); BACoN VCFs are rewritten. Checkpoints record each step's own output signature, and a result is only reused when its output is still the file it wrote: a sample returning to a sheet can no longer pick up reads another sample wrote over. Switching a sample between single-end and paired (or fasta and fastq) removes the other shape's files. BBDuk's paired outputs are checked mate against mate, like minimap2's (a desynchronised pair fails the sample); mates named .1 / .2 ( fastq-dump --readids ) pair; the unpaired-reads file of fasterq-dump --split-3 next to its pair is skipped with a warning; a file cannot pair with a link to itself, and files that look like mates but do not pair are warned about. Stale fastp reports are removed on rerun and for samples that fail at baiting. The report and MultiQC drop the circular-contigs column (no short-read assembler flags circles) and say that read pairs were kept whole when either mate matched.
items.title: RASHER: Bait, Assemble and Compare Illumina short reads

items.summary: International observation systems reveal a consequential possibility: scientific information can be generated, validated, and circulated across institutional and political boundaries without requiring a single authority over all observations or a uniform distribution of capacities . Yet the existence of data-sharing protocols does not by itself establish shared understanding, mutual trust, legitimate reuse, or equitable participation in the production of knowledge . This discussion paper investigates the technical, epistemic, and institutional conditions under which global observation and knowledge infrastructures might be constructed and sustained . Drawing on meteorological and oceanographic cooperation, it distinguishes observational coverage, data availability, interoperability, interpretation, and collective authority. It proposes a preliminary federated research architecture connecting situated observation nodes, provenance and quality records, semantic and model translation, distributed computation, access governance, correction, and contestation. It treats mathematical, physical, social, and normative languages as historically formed manifestations and practices within generative-relational systems, distinguishing their conditional formal invariance from claims to universally identical representation. It further investigates why actors situated in different generative and institutional histories may interpret shared evidence differently, and proposes a bounded research vocabulary for mutually workable norms, continued disagreement, and rule revision without assuming epistemic consensus. The paper conceptualizes trust as a historically constituted relation supported in part by verifiable commitments, reciprocal inquiry, accountable institutions, and effective remedy rather than as a property supplied by cryptography or open data alone. It further specifies prospective services for common knowledge creation and circulation, generalized translation of heterogeneous generative-relational contexts, and traceable transformations of distinct forms of value. A staged validation design differentiates synthetic policy gates, cross-node scientific comparison, productive-capacity trials, and site-dependent ecological and institutional review. A cross-layer assessment profile separates technical interchange, scientific warrant, claimed competent authority, and effective contestation, without deriving legal or ethical legitimacy from technical success. It also examines epistemic and infrastructural asymmetries, the sensitivity of ecological and community data, the incompleteness of model-based assimilation, and the risks of concentrating interpretive authority in highly capable AI systems. Global weather and ocean observation provide instructive but bounded cases, not evidence that all knowledge should be made public or placed under centralized control. The proposed programme remains exploratory and separates conceptual architecture from implemented infrastructure, independent empirical assessment, and normative justification.
items.title: Global Observation and Knowledge Infrastructures: A Study of Collective Inquiry across Heterogeneous Relational Systems

items.summary: Full FHOPS 1.0.1 rolling-horizon re-run outputs, with the M7 cold-MIP re-run replacing the MIP arm. What changed since v1.1.0-rerun M7 cold-MIP re-run ( 9f0ab69 ): the 117 MIP runs were re-run with the simulated-annealing phase idle (1,800 s stage 1, 900 s earliness, one Gurobi thread per window, 36 windows in parallel), together with the size-40 7,200 s baseline sensitivity runs and the resumed SA run for ni_40_sub112_lock1 . The re-run did not confirm the contention hypothesis. Matching 603,700 per-solve Gurobi records, its work rate was 8.4% higher (median 0.523 → 0.567 work units/s), yet it produced more failures: no-solution windows 9 → 32, empty windows 18 → 39. 20 of 117 runs changed; the long lock1 trajectories diverge, the short ones are identical. The counts describe a time-limited solve, not a fixed property of each instance. Contents data/output/rerun_v101_gurobi/ — SA arm (117 runs) and the original MIP arm. data/output/rerun_v101_gurobi_alone/ — the M7 cold-MIP re-run (117 runs). data/output/rerun_v101_gurobi_sensitivity_* — 7,200 s baseline sensitivity runs. Per-run JSON summaries, stitched assignment tables, solver logs, summary.csv , and the runner / probe / calibration scripts. The paper built from this deposit is UBC-FRESH/fhops-cjfr-rolling-horizon ; its analysis script replays every stitched plan against the full scenario.

items.summary: This deposit is the numerical companion to “One-Sided p-Explicit Stability for High-Order Cut Finite Element Nitsche Methods” by Erik Burman, Peter Hansbo, Mats G. Larson and Karl Larsson. It contains Python experiment code, case parameters, compact reference data, reproducibility instructions and the Numerical Verification Guide. The implementation uses two-dimensional triangular P p finite elements and CPU-based dense linear algebra. The studies cover polynomial continuation, one-sided flux estimates, penalty thresholds, convergence, numerical precision, Schwarz comparisons and exact tube certificates. The compact data retain 4,959 reference observations, 239 failed criteria and 22 tables, including known accuracy flags, the original solver-stopping failure and unresolved higher-degree attempts. Selected validation covers 15 numerical commands across ten study families; it is not a rerun of the full 257-command campaign or an audit of the omitted raw archives. Raw run archives and manuscript sources are not included. Detailed run records and exact certificates can be regenerated using the documented commands. The continuation and tube studies are tested on Apple Silicon macOS and Linux x86-64. The remaining supplied validation studies require the documented Linux configuration with a 64-bit longdouble significand and multiprocessing fork. The package includes file-integrity checks and pinned dependencies. Licensing is component-specific: Python code and software documentation are licensed under MIT; numerical data and the Numerical Verification Guide are licensed under CC BY 4.0. See LICENSE for the precise scope. AI assistance and author responsibility are disclosed in README.md. This documentation update aligns the guide’s references with the revised manuscript numbering. Numerical code, case inputs, reference data and dependency pins are unchanged; numerical tests were not rerun for this update. Source repository: KarlLarssonUmU/one-sided-hp-cutfem Archived commit: bae06c644b21f723ee636ed67663c99e06004cfd .
items.title: Numerical Companion to One-Sided p-Explicit Stability for High-Order Cut Finite Element Nitsche Methods

items.summary: DIGITAL TWINS AND AI CLOSED-LOOP CONTROL FOR NANOROBOTIC PHARMACEUTICAL MANUFACTURING AT THE LIMIT Digital Twins x AI Process Control x Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Quality This high-density English research monograph develops a falsification-oriented architecture for digital twins and AI closed-loop control in nonclinical nanorobotic pharmaceutical manufacturing research. Its central question is whether a process-state estimator can predict quality failure under raw-material, flow, sensor and equipment drift before the failure occurs, rather than merely replaying historical data as an attractive dashboard. The governing evidence object is the Falsifiable Manufacturing Twin. It binds a declared physical state, observation model, uncertainty envelope, process and sensor versions, candidate and executed control actions, external critical-quality-attribute measurements, abstention, fallback and terminal batch fate. A twin earns authority only while new physical evidence can contradict it. Failed, stopped, out-of-distribution and externally falsified batches remain in the denominator. The monograph compares fixed recipes, statistical process control, tuned PID, strong non-learning model predictive control and AI under equal sensing, energy, constraints and operator access. It treats calibrated ignorance as a successful behavior: an unsupported state must cause abstention, return to a separately qualified safe recipe or stop. External CQA evidence always outranks the model. The volume contains 30 distinct mathematical research plates, 82 chapters, 410 independently paginated section studies, 200 detailed Research Gates and 33 genuinely distinguishable Phoenix Answer Embryos. Every Gate begins with a large deep-navy bold question and continues with a blind protocol, evidence package, competing explanation, hard stop and successor fork.

items.summary: Resilience and Recovery in a \mathbb{Z}_5-Graded NonAssociative System: A Computational Study of Constraint Disruption and Re-Stabilization C. J. Tully, Independent Researcher Engineer, Australia   https://orcid.org/0009 - 0007 - 5661 - 7332 chloetully5@gmail.com   25 th October 2026 Abstract We present a particle-based simulator whose interaction rule on a five-dimensional sector is given by a non-associative, \mathbb{Z}_5-graded multiplication table with golden-ratio weights. The system is subject to spatial forces under several model choices and is equipped with hard gates (velocity clipping and minimum-distance floors). We define a coherence metric on the graded sector and an associator norm that quantifies local failure of associativity. In a controlled perturbation experiment, a sudden shock applied to half the particles at step 75 produces an immediate drop in coherence (0.968 \to 0.511) and a sharp rise in the associator norm (0.008 \to 0.108). The associator continues to rise for approximately ten steps after the external shock has ended, reaching a peak of 0.224, after which both quantities relax: by step 149 coherence has recovered to 0.885   the associator has returned to 0.013. The result demonstrates that, under the chosen force law and hard gates, the graded interaction is capable of re-establishing lowassociator, high-coherence configurations after a severe disruption. We discuss the finding in relation to organizational closure, path dependence, and the distinction between structural and dynamical aspects of self-maintenance. Keywords: Graded algebras, non-associativity, organizational closure, resilience, path dependence, computational models, TT-G41
items.title: Resilience and Recovery in a \mathbb{Z}_5-Graded NonAssociative System: A Computational Study of Constraint Disruption and Re-Stabilization

items.summary: Highlights of the Study This comprehensive review examines the fatigue behaviour of load-bearing polymeric bone scaffolds , addressing a critical but comparatively underexplored aspect of bone tissue engineering. It evaluates the mechanisms governing fatigue damage and systematically examines how polymer characteristics, microstructure, reinforcing materials, scaffold topology, manufacturing methods, loading conditions, body fluids, and tissue ingrowth influence fatigue performance, with particular emphasis on translating polymeric scaffolds toward reliable load-bearing clinical applications. Key findings: 🟢 Fatigue failure mechanisms: Polymeric scaffolds can undergo both mechanical and thermal fatigue. Repeated cyclic loading causes residual-strain accumulation, stiffness and peak-stress reduction, crack development, and hysteretic heating, which can progressively degrade polymer chains and ultimately cause structural failure. 🟢 Low- and high-cycle fatigue: Low-cycle fatigue generally occurs under relatively high stresses and involves repeated plastic deformation, whereas high-cycle fatigue develops over much larger numbers of cycles under lower stress levels and is primarily associated with elastic deformation and progressive material degradation. 🟢 Material and microstructural effects: Polymer fatigue resistance is strongly governed by molecular and microstructural characteristics. Increased crystallinity, molecular weight, and molecular-chain entanglement can improve fatigue resistance, emphasizing the importance of selecting and tailoring the polymer microstructure for load-bearing scaffolds. 🟢 Reinforcement strategy: Incorporating ceramic or metallic reinforcing phases can substantially improve the fatigue performance of polymeric scaffolds by redistributing applied loads and dissipating energy that would otherwise contribute to polymer deformation and heat generation. 🟢 Hydroxyapatite reinforcement: Incorporation of 15 wt% hydroxyapatite increased the fatigue limit of PLA scaffolds by approximately 17%, while also improving compressive modulus, crack resistance, and hysteresis energy compared with unreinforced PLA. 🟢 Scaffold topology: Pore architecture plays a decisive role in fatigue behaviour by controlling stress distribution and stress concentration. Even scaffolds fabricated from the same polymer and having comparable porosity can exhibit substantially different fatigue lives when their pore geometry and filament arrangement are changed. 🟢 Topology-dependent fatigue life: Among 3D-printed PLA scaffolds with comparable porosity, the tetragonal topology achieved a fatigue life of approximately 4400 cycles, outperforming hexagonal and wheel-like structures at approximately 3200 and 2500 cycles, respectively. 🟢 Advanced scaffold architectures: TPMS, Voronoi, functionally graded, auxetic, and other irregular architectures offer promising approaches for load-bearing scaffolds. TPMS structures are particularly attractive because their smooth transitions at strut junctions may reduce stress concentrations, although their polymer fatigue behaviour remains insufficiently investigated. 🟢 Bone-inspired architecture: Bio-inspired scaffold design can substantially improve fatigue performance. Increasing the thickness of transverse rod-like struts in bone-inspired structures was reported to enhance fatigue life by approximately 10–100 times with relatively minor effects on density and stiffness. 🟢 Porosity–strength trade-off: Increasing porosity promotes permeability, vascularization, cell migration, and tissue ingrowth but simultaneously reduces scaffold stiffness, strength, and load-bearing capacity. Therefore, successful scaffold design requires balancing biological benefits against fatigue and mechanical integrity. 🟢 Stress concentration: Geometrical discontinuities and sharp pore corners create localized stress concentrations that accelerate fatigue damage. Circular pores can provide more uniform stress distribu
items.title: Fatigue behavior of load-bearing polymeric bone scaffolds: A review

items.summary: The rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence in agriculture has improved the production of crops, monitoring of the overall process of farming, resource management, and what type of resources will be used for more and better production of the crops in today's era. So, for that AI helps us a lot. The reason behind the use of AI in farming is that better production is what each and every farmer wants. Transparency-like, if the crops got damages, then the farmers have clear and accurate knowledge about the failure of the crop. Explainable Artificial Intelligence addresses this challenge by providing clear, interpretable insights into how the AI system makes decisions. This paper explores how AI is beneficial in farming, focusing on several techniques such as feature importance, visualization, and rule-based explanations that improve decision-making in crop management. This also explores several tools-like, the weather condition, equipment required that gives more than expected outcome, and much more. By this study, some of the features I want to add through technology which helps farmers for better production. The addition of technology in farming enhances transparency, trust, and sustainability in modern farming practices. The importance of XAI in agriculture forms the foundation of this research paper, which intends to present various explanation techniques and study how they will lead to trustworthy decision-making in crop management. This study also presents the use of technological tools such as climate monitoring systems, automated equipment, soil sensors, and data-driven forecasting models that work in harmony with XAI for delivering superior results. XAI provides clear and understandable explanations-such that farmers would not only use the AI-based tool but fully trust and utilize it to truly make farming smarter and more resilient.

items.summary: This record accompanies the manuscript “Feedback Leakage in Historical Continuous Integration Test-Selection Evaluation”. It contains author-created replay and analysis code, frozen protocol descriptions, aggregate experimental results, figure source data, portable plotting scripts, provenance records, and verification information. The materials cover the industrial feedback comparison, first-failure and statistical analyses, exploratory adaptive reserve, recorded-cost analyses, and bounded external/reconstruction studies. Third-party raw archives, normalized input rows, and per-action selected test or row identities are excluded. Source locations, versions, hashes, and access conditions are documented so that permitted inputs can be obtained separately. The package supports two levels of reproduction: (1) computations that can be directly reproduced using the included summaries, and (2) selection replays that require separately obtained external inputs. It does not claim to provide a self-contained, one-click rerun for every historical execution. Author-created code is licensed under MIT. items.summary: Multimodal $ΔΔG$ predictors integrating protein language models with inverse-folding representations achieve strong in-distribution accuracy on the Megascale dataset but exhibit limited robustness on out-of-distribution (OOD) proteins, persistent forward-reverse bias on paired-mutation benchmarks, and under-representation of rare stabilizing mutations. Existing approaches address these limitations primarily through additional architectural components, leaving optimization-level intervention comparatively underexplored. We introduce a constraint-aware optimization framework combining Balanced Mean Squared Error, a Siamese anti-symmetric regularizer, and a novel OOD-margin consistency loss on the per-position feature representation, requiring no architectural changes to the SPURS backbone. Across eleven benchmarks and three random seeds, the framework improves Spearman correlation on S669 from 0.486 to 0.540 ($σ=0.002$ across seeds), matching the published SPURS baseline (0.50) without architectural modification, and on S461 from 0.653 to 0.711, with consistent smaller gains on five additional OOD datasets. A controlled diagnostic on Ssym reveals that anti-symmetric training does not eliminate systematic forward-reverse bias, indicating that gains arise through implicit regularization rather than exact thermodynamic constraint enforcement.
items.title: Constraint-Aware Optimization for Robust Protein Stability Prediction

items.summary: This record contains the replication data and R code for the study “How much does the publication universe matter? Source discontinuities and panel selection in OpenAlex” by Vladislav Bína and Jiří Přibil. The package includes OpenAlex source-by-year counts for 2010–2025 retrieved on 10–11 October 2026, supplementary OpenAlex and Crossref aggregate counts retrieved on 23 October 2026, a provenance-limited earlier archive of annual totals, and twelve annotated illustrative record checks. It also provides eight R scripts, expected numerical results, numerical inputs to the figures, and English documentation. The default workflow reproduces the saved-data analyses offline using base R. It covers publication growth, continuity panels, source turnover, panel-selection timing, population layers, and sensitivity to comparison horizons and endpoints. items.summary: Water scarcity is becoming a growing problem worldwide due to the expansion of industry, population growth and climate change, and the need for clean and potable water is becoming increasingly important. Traditional wastewater treatment techniques such as sedimentation, filtration, and chlorination often fail to remove emerging contaminants (ECs), such as pharmaceuticals, microplastics, heavy metals, and sometimes create toxic byproducts. Thus, nanotechnology has come up as a novel solution with materials of incredible surface area, tunable reactivity and adsorption capacities. In recent years, a paradigm change towards sustainability has led to the creation of "green" or biogenic nanomaterials. The green nanomaterials are synthesized from renewable biological resources like plant extracts and microbial consortia, which reduce environmental footprints, the use of hazardous chemicals and provide cost-effective remediation. The present review covers all the recent developments in the use of green nanomaterials such as metal/metal oxide nanoparticles (Ag, TiO₂, Fe₃O₄, ZnO), carbon-based nanostructures and bio-inspired nanocomposites in wastewater monitoring and remediation. Systematically, the main mechanisms of contaminant removal, such as physical adsorption, chemical adsorption, photocatalytic degradation, electrochemical reduction and advanced membrane filtration are explored. In addition, the incorporation of very sensitive nanosensors for real-time environmental monitoring is discussed. Recent computational methods, such as Molecular Dynamics (MD), Density Functional Theory (DFT), and Machine Learning (ML), are emphasized as key tools to translate experimental design into application, and to predict the efficacy and toxicity of nanoparticles. Finally, this review critically examines the issues of scalability, economic viability and nanotoxicity, and outlines the path for sustainable implementation of nanotechnology in water management on a global scale. Graphical Abstract: Comprehensive framework for green nanomaterials in wastewater treatment, illustrating synthesis pathways from biological sources, removal mechanisms, and a critical overview of benefits, limitations, and future applications. Reproduced from Sustainable Chemistry for the Environment 10 (2025) 100238, under the Creative Commons CC BY‑NC‑ND 4.0 licence (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/) [1] .
tags: Environmental Sustainability, Sustainable Development, Renewable Energy, Climate Change, Circular Ec
items.title: Sustainable Innovations in Green Nanomaterials for Contaminated Water Management and Remediation

items.summary: Genetic mutations frequently disrupt protein structure, stability, and solubility, acting as primary drivers for a wide spectrum of diseases. Despite the critical importance of these molecular alterations, existing computational models often lack interpretability, and fail to integrate essential physicochemical interaction. To overcome these limitations, we propose SheafLapNet, a unified predictive framework grounded in the mathematical theory of Topological Deep Learning (TDL) and Persistent Sheaf Laplacian (PSL). Unlike standard Topological Data Analysis (TDA) tools such as persistent homology, which are often insensitive to heterogeneous information, PSL explicitly encodes specific physical and chemical information such as partial charges directly into the topological analysis. SheafLapNet synergizes these sheaf-theoretic invariants with advanced protein transformer features and auxiliary physical descriptors to capture intrinsic molecular interactions in a multiscale and mechanistic manner. To validate our framework, we employ rigorous benchmarks for both regression and classification tasks. For stability prediction, we utilize the comprehensive S2648 and S350 datasets. For solubility prediction, we employ the PON-Sol2 dataset, which provides annotations for increased, decreased, or neutral solubility changes. By integrating these multi-perspective features, SheafLapNet achieves state-of-the-art performance across these diverse benchmarks, demonstrating that sheaf-theoretic modeling significantly enhances both interpretability and generalizability in predicting mutation-induced structural and functional changes.
items.title: Persistent Sheaf Laplacian Analysis of Protein Stability and Solubility Changes upon Mutation

items.summary: The work builds a foundation of physics from a single assumption: everything is a process, and a process is an ideal sine; its centre, the balance, is the observer. Only the square — intensity without phase — passes between levels; from this arise dimensions, the arrow of time, the quantum and the standard. On this basis stable particles are built as standing waves together with their galactic analogues, the initial rules of quantum mechanics and relativity are derived, and the constants are linked to a single number — the speed of light. Agreement with experiment is at the level of a few percent; the model attributes the discrepancies to the imperfection of the standard. Main results The four stable particles (neutrino, electron, neutron, proton) are the four stable states of a standing wave; masses from the speed of light alone: electron +0.7 %, nucleons about −3 % [result given hypotheses]. The Born rule, the randomness of a single outcome, the 2√2 limit in the Bell test, spin ½ and g = 2 [result]. The Lorentz transformation from the “speed budget” c² = v² + v_int², the Klein — Gordon and Schrödinger equations, Schwarzschild gravitational time dilation and the light deflection of 1.75″ [result]. Similarity of the small and the large with the step c⁴: the image of the neutron is the stellar mass of the Milky Way (5.5·10¹⁰ versus (6.1 ± 1.1)·10¹⁰ solar masses) [hypothesis, numerical agreement]. The large end is built by the same logic as the microworld: the construction yields the Hubble constant H₀ = 1/(5c²) ≈ 68.7 km/s/Mpc and the smallest acceleration of galaxies a₀ = 1/(10πc) [result given hypotheses]. The gravitational constant G ≈ c^(−6/5) (0.8 %); the mass of the Universe and the scale of dark energy are expressed through c [hypothesis]. The fine-structure constant has been found as the number 1/α ≈ 4·(c/2π)^(1/5) (0.22 %); its meaning is open [observation]. Limitations: the accuracy is percent-level, not parts per million; the standard and several constants remain open questions. The status of each statement is given in the text. Revision dated 2026-10-24:   Version 24.2 continues to unwind the process from the large end (Part VI). The qualitative descriptions have been refined: the black hole is the centre of mass of the whole construction of a galaxy, and its mass is mainly dark matter; the process itself is not entirely hidden — we see its manifestation in dark matter and spin. The quantum of the large end is described as the passage of the spin through the point of balance, where zero and the limit are one and the same; the flat rotation curve as one and the same energy level at every radius of the disc. The birth of baryons is described: the rotation and acceleration of dark matter, the limit of tempo 1/c, the constant birth of particles in a galaxy. A qualitative explanation has been found of why the fractal transfer of the parameters of the neutron gives a link precisely with the stellar mass of the Milky Way. A qualitative explanation of coupling at another level is given: in a galaxy two different processes of mass formation — dark matter and baryons — are linked in space by rotation, not in the dimension of mass, so here the coupling is visible, whereas in the neutron it is hidden beyond mass. The abstract, the summary of Part VI and the register have been brought into agreement; the changes are made in all three languages.         Работа строит основу физики из одного допущения: всё — процесс, а процесс — идеальный синус; его центр, баланс, — наблюдатель. Между уровнями проходит только квадрат — интенсивность без фазы; отсюда рождаются измерения, стрела времени, квант и эталон. На этой основе построены стабильные частицы как стоячие волны и их галактические аналоги, выведены исходные

items.summary: The relentless pursuit of modeling quantum many-body systems has exposed a profound epistemic and technological schism in modern physics. As the dimension of the Hilbert space expands exponentially with each additional particle, direct computational modeling via classical state vectors becomes a physical impossibility. Concurrently, the physical realization of fault-tolerant Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) is stymied by persistent decoherence, fragile topological phases, and exorbitant error correction overheads. In response to this paradigm, a disparate array of mathematical techniques and classical computational heuristics have emerged, often mis-categorized under the broad, imprecise umbrella of "quantum computing" or "quantum simulation." This exhaustive report serves as the formal proposal and rigorous justification for the establishment of a new, distinct scientific discipline: Quantum Mathematics and Quantum Emulation. By synthesizing avant-garde mathematical constructs—including non-commutative geometry, von Neumann operator algebras, and the Connes-Kreimer Hopf algebra of renormalization—with High-Performance Computing (HPC) techniques such as the Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) and Projected Entangled Pair States (PEPS), this field systematically truncates quantum state spaces for deterministic emulation. Architected by Syed Abraham Ahmed, Founder and CEO of Lifeline AI, this document serves as the synergetic collection of prior art and modern innovation to  create the field of Quantum Mathematics and Quantum Emulation . This document formally synthesizes these isolated mathematical and computational breakthroughs into a unified discipline by acknowledging the foundational prior art, in the noble pursuit of scientific integrity, accuracy, and logical justification. It is fundamentally necessary to correctly re-categorize these algorithmic efforts away from quantum hardware simulation and unify rooting them in rigorous mathematical compression—ensuring continued scientific merit and progress for distinguishing the accurate categorization of research funding mechanisms. Furthermore, the development of the novel field of Quantum Mathematics provides an actionable and definitive pathway to empower the future of scientific discovery, utilizing existing supercomputing constructs to bypass the limitations of physical quantum hardware, and champion the synergistic fusion of these existing elements to unlock entirely novel computational paradigms. Part 1 establishes the historical and taxonomic necessity of this classification, while Part 2 details the rigorous sub-Planckian algebraic architectures required for its execution. Ultimately, by rooting the existing siloed unification of Quantum Mathematics away from the physical Quantum hardware simulation, this structural re-categorization is a fundamental necessity for both scientific integrity and provides the computational pathway to bypass hardware limitations and compute the quantum realm using existing supercomputing powerhouse constructs.
items.title: The Creation of Quantum Mathematics and Quantum Emulation

items.summary: Version 2.0, October 24, 2026: Empirical Revision Substantially revised Paper I to incorporate exploratory geochemical validation using published EarthChem and Alcott et al. (2026) measurements. Added EBA-1/EBA-2 sulfur-isotope change-point analysis, independent phosphorus and redox comparisons, alternative-boundary null testing, and blocked predictive model comparisons. The core source–sink hypothesis is retained, while claims concerning a uniquely identified tipping point, regional diachrony, and demonstrated feedback causation are explicitly qualified. The revision includes updated literature context, methodological limitations, and supplementary analytical materials. Supersedes version 1.0 as the current research statement while preserving the original publication history. The Great Oxidation Event (GOE) reflects the evolving balance between biological oxygen production, reductant consumption, atmospheric photochemistry, and ocean–sediment exchange. This paper develops a basin-resolved source–sink threshold framework in which regional oxygenation responses may differ despite shared atmospheric forcing. Version 2.0 extends the original theoretical framework through exploratory quantitative analysis of published EBA-1 and EBA-2 drill-core geochemistry, including sulfur mass-independent fractionation, phosphorus distributions, organic carbon, and redox-sensitive trace elements. An exploratory sulfur-isotope change point was identified at 1,336.87 m in EBA-2. Independent geochemical measurements exhibit substantial variation across this interval. However, depth-controlled null comparisons and blocked out-of-sample prediction do not establish a uniquely coordinated tipping-point transition. Predictive improvements are restricted to selected indicators and depend partly on baseline specification. These findings preserve the source–sink feedback framework as a testable explanation for nonlinear and spatially heterogeneous oxygenation while distinguishing theoretical plausibility from demonstrated causal dynamics. The revised manuscript provides empirical comparisons, competing-model evaluations, explicit limitations, and falsification criteria for future research. Part of the Planetary Convexity Series, Paper I.
items.title: Diachronous Oxygenation as a Planetary Tipping Point
